title: Conditional probability and independence check
scenario_markdown: In a financial portfolio, the probability of Tech sector growth is $P(A) = 0.40$, Health sector growth is $P(B) = 0.60$, and simultaneous growth in both is $P(A \cap B) = 0.24$. Find the conditional probability of Tech sector growth given Health sector growth, $P(A \mid B)$.
assumptions: Conditioning event has positive probability: P(B) = 0.60 > 0
Valid joint probability: P(A cap B) = 0.24 <= P(B)
Independent events because P(A cap B) = P(A)*P(B)

approval.notes: Reviewed derivation: P(A|B) = P(A cap B) / P(B) = 0.24 / 0.60 = 0.40 = P(A). Proves statistical independence.

stages.prompt_markdown: Which formula defines the conditional probability $P(A \mid B)$?

options.hint_markdown: Which event is given as already having occurred?
Conditional probability reduces the sample space to the conditioning event B.

stages.explanation_markdown: Conditional probability $P(A \mid B)$ evaluates the likelihood of $A$ within the reduced sample space of $B$: $\frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate $P(A \mid B) = \frac{0.24}{0.60}$. Enter as a decimal, percent, or fraction.
Are events A (Tech growth) and B (Health growth) statistically independent?

options.text_markdown: Yes, because $P(A \mid B) = P(A) = 0.40$ (learning that B occurred does not change the probability of A).

options.hint_markdown: Independent events with positive probabilities MUST overlap ($P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B) > 0$).

options.text_markdown: No, because sectors in the same economy are never independent.
options.hint_markdown: Judge by the mathematical condition: does $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$?

stages.explanation_markdown: Events are independent if and only if $P(A \mid B) = P(A)$, or equivalently $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$. Here $0.40 \times 0.60 = 0.24$, so they are independent.
